fields.Front: How are entities and relationships drawn in Crow's Foot notation, and why does the instructor teach it?
fields.Back: Entity: a BOX with the name in a header and the attributes listed inside, keys underlined/marked PK - no ovals. Relationship: just a LINE between the entities - no diamond - whose end shows both the cardinality and the participation. She teaches it so you recognise it elsewhere (most professional tools use it and it looks close to UML), but 'for this course I'd prefer you use the other notation with the rectangles and the ovals' - Chen.

fields.Front: List the four Crow's Foot line ends with their symbols and Chen equivalents.
fields.Back:
o< circle + crow's foot = ZERO OR MORE: many side, partial, (0,N)
|< bar + crow's foot = ONE OR MORE: many side, total, (1,N)
|| bar + bar = ONE AND ONLY ONE: one side, total, (1,1)
o| circle + bar = ZERO OR ONE: one side, partial, (0,1)

fields.Front: APPLICATION: translate A ||-------o< B into Chen cardinality, participation and (min, max).
fields.Back: 1:N from A to B. B end: every B has exactly one A - total, (1,1) beside B. A end: an A has zero or more Bs - partial, (0,N) beside A. In Chen you would write 1 beside A, N beside B, a double line at B and a single line at A.

fields.Front: Read the slide's four Crow's Foot examples as the instructor does.
fields.Back:
STUDENT ||----|| SEAT: one-to-one, total both sides - a student fills one and only one seat and every seat is filled.
INSTRUCTOR ||----|< COURSE: an instructor teaches one or many courses (at least one); a course is taught by one and only one instructor.
STUDENT >|----|< COURSE: many-to-many, each side at least one.
PROFESSOR ||----o< SECTION: a professor teaches zero or many sections (they might be doing research); a section is taught by one and only one professor.

fields.Front: DVD store: name the three entities with their attributes and say why DVDCOPY is separate from MOVIE.
fields.Back: CUSTOMER (CustomerID, FirstName, LastName) - customers may never have purchased before; MOVIE (MovieID, Title, Year); DVDCOPY (DVDID, HomeStore) - the physical disc. Separate because 'a movie might be Star Wars, but we might have five copies of Star Wars DVDs. A customer rents a DVD; they don't rent a movie.'

fields.Front: DVD store: give both ends of 'currently renting' (CUSTOMER to DVDCOPY) with her reasoning.
fields.Back:
DVDCOPY end: ZERO OR MORE (o<) - a customer might not be renting any DVDs, or could be renting many.
CUSTOMER end: ZERO OR ONE (o|) - a DVD may be rented by nobody ('if it's a crappy movie') but only one person can currently be renting it.
In Chen: CUSTOMER (0,1) --- (0,N) DVDCOPY, 1:N and partial on both sides.

fields.Front: DVD store: give both ends of 'is a' (DVDCOPY to MOVIE) with her reasoning.
fields.Back:
DVDCOPY end: ONE OR MORE (|<) - the store only keeps track of a movie if it has at least one copy, and a popular movie has many.
MOVIE end: ONE AND ONLY ONE (||) - a DVD has to be exactly one type of movie: no blank DVDs, and a DVD cannot have two movies on it.
In Chen: DVDCOPY (1,1) --- is a --- (1,N) MOVIE, N:1 and total on both sides.

fields.Front: draw.io demo: what Crow's Foot line did the instructor choose for CUSTOMER currently renting CAR, and why?
fields.Back: CUSTOMER o|-------o| CAR: optional one to optional one. A customer might not be renting a car and would only rent one car at a time; a car does not have to be rented and can currently be rented by only one customer. She uses the Entity Relation shapes 'because they actually have ones for the crow's feet' with ready-made connectors.

fields.Front: APPLICATION: read the planets diagram ends - planet/star and planet/moon.
fields.Back: A planet circles ZERO OR ONE star ('if it's just an asteroid it might not be circling any'); a star has ZERO OR MANY planets; a planet has ZERO OR MANY moons; a moon orbits AT LEAST ONE planet.

fields.Text: In a Crow's Foot line end the mark closer to the {{c1::entity}} gives the maximum, i.e. the {{c1::cardinality}} (bar = one, crow's foot = many); the mark closer to the {{c1::middle of the line}} gives the minimum, i.e. the participation (circle = 0/optional, bar = 1/total).
